title: VH Health QA Finding
description: Schema for a single agent-discovered QA finding. The finding is materialized as Markdown under docs/qa-findings/<date>-<slug>.md. The frontmatter of that Markdown file MUST validate against this schema. Free-form prose (root cause hypothesis, retrospective notes) goes in the Markdown body.

run_id.description: Orchestrator run id this finding came out of (matches qa-runs/<run_id>/).

git_sha.description: Repo SHA at the time of the run.

seed_version.description: 16-char hash of the seeder source files at run time, taken from qa_seed_meta.seed_version.

base_url.description: The HTTP base of the system under test (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:5206 for local smoke env, or https://vh-api.dalekdefender for the live deploy).

tenant_id.description: Tenant UUID under which the scenario ran (defaults to 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001).

scenario.description: Short human label for what the agent was trying to do, e.g. 'patient books appointment under unicode name'.

command.description: The exact shell command the harness executed, copy-pasteable.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the failing command. 0 is allowed when the failure was content-based (e.g. a 200 response that contained a wrong field).

severity.description: Triage severity. critical: data loss / PHI exposure / auth bypass. high: workflow blocker. medium: UX friction or workaround exists. low: cosmetic. info: observation, no action required.

area.description: Functional area for routing to the right reviewer.

repro_steps.description: Ordered, copy-pasteable reproduction steps. Include env vars, curl commands, or PowerShell invocations as needed.

expected.description: What the harness expected to happen.

actual.description: What actually happened (HTTP status, error body, stack trace excerpt).

artifacts.description: Paths (relative to repo root) of supporting artifacts under qa-runs/<run_id>/.

confidence.description: How confident the finding is a real bug vs an env / test issue. Low-confidence findings should still be filed but flagged for triage.

first_seen_run.description: run_id where this finding was first observed; identical to run_id on the first writeup, may differ on duplicates.
